description: Canonical source -> byte-identical copies. Every checker that ships in three places (the plugin's own scripts/, the scaffold template, and each gold fixture) is declared here so the copies can be regenerated and asserted instead of hand-maintained. A copy that drifts is a stale fork: the fixture stops testing what the live script does, and scaffolded repos inherit a bug that was already fixed upstream. Regenerate: bash skills/repo/_contract/scripts/sync-contract-scripts.sh. Assert: same script with --check.
rationale: Observed: skills/repo/_contract/fixtures/*/scripts/check-feature-equivalence.sh sat on a pre-fix revision of scripts/check-feature-equivalence.sh (SC2055 single-bracket form) for as long as fixtures were outside the lint scope, and templates/check-manifest-version-alignment.sh.tmpl never received --allow-pending-release or the BSD-sed usage() fix. Neither was detected because nothing compared them.

groups.note: Fully portable — repo type is detected at runtime, so the plugin, the template and every fixture run the identical file.
Portable. Repo-specific behaviour is guarded by directory existence (skills/documentation/, core/capabilities/), not by editing the copy.

The plugin's own scripts/check-agent-drift.sh is deliberately NOT the canonical source here: it is a 14-line wrapper around this repo's scripts/validate-skill-frontmatter.py, while the contract version is the portable generic checker. Two different scripts that share a name, not a fork.

Template had forked: it lacked --allow-pending-release, directional ahead/behind drift detection, and the BSD-sed usage() fix (GNU-only `# \?` leaves the comment prefixes visible on macOS). Scaffolded repos were inheriting all three defects.
The template is canonical because repo-scaffold renders it; the fixture is the rendered result and carries no substitutions.

The scaffold template is GENERATED from the live registry schema by lifting this repo's owner/name out into placeholders. Declared before the fixture group so one sync pass propagates registry -> template -> fixtures.

Same chain for the registry instance. Platform capability truth is repo-independent, so a scaffolded repo should start from the verified statuses rather than a copy that rotted. This link is why the corrected OpenCode symlink guidance now reaches the template automatically.
Rendered into fixtures with GITHUB_OWNER/REPO_NAME substituted, so the copies are NOT byte-identical. Declared with substitutions so the check compares the rendered form.
Platform capability truth is repo-independent; only the install/repo strings vary, and those are the substitutions.

capability_mirror_roots.note: platform-targets.json carries a DERIVED capability mirror generated from that tree's core/capabilities/platforms.json. Re-rendering a fixture registry (which happens whenever the live registry is corrected) leaves its mirror stale, so the sync entry point regenerates these too. Under --check nothing is done here: each fixture's own check-platform-targets.sh run already fails on a stale mirror, and that is the message you want to see.
